definitions.explanation: A raised structure or table used for religious rituals, offerings, or memorial services. Used across religious traditions including Shinto, Buddhism, and Christianity.

examples.japanese: {祭壇|さいだん}に{花|はな}を{供|そな}える。
examples.english: To place flowers on the altar.

examples.japanese: {教会|きょうかい}の{祭壇|さいだん}の{前|まえ}で{誓|ちか}いを{立|た}てた。
examples.english: They made their vows before the altar of the church.

examples.japanese: {故人|こじん}を{偲|しの}んで、{祭壇|さいだん}に{写真|しゃしん}と{遺品|いひん}が{飾|かざ}られていた。
examples.english: In memory of the deceased, photographs and personal belongings were displayed on the altar.

notes:
USAGE:
Used broadly across religious contexts. In Japanese funerals, a {祭壇|さいだん} is set up with the deceased's photograph, flowers, and offerings. Also refers to altars in churches, shrines, and temples.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祭壇|さいだん}に{供|そな}える: to make an offering at the altar
- {祭壇|さいだん}を{設|もう}ける: to set up an altar
- {祭壇|さいだん}に{手|て}を{合|あ}わせる: to put one's hands together (pray) at the altar
- {葬儀|そうぎ}の{祭壇|さいだん}: funeral altar
